newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL HAVE HISTORY ON THEIR SIDE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL HAVE HISTORY ON THEIR SIDE.

text.p: If recent history is any guide then Liverpool have a better than even chance of winning the English championship this season.
The pointer to Liverpool's success is the league table at the turn of the year, midway point in the arduous season.

Eleven times in the last 20 seasons, the team top on New Year's Eve have gone on to win the title, and Liverpool will be at the head of the table on December 31 irrespective of the outcome of their match against Southampton at The Dell on Sunday.
Liverpool, who have not won the title since 1990, have rarely buckled in the second half of a season in which they were first on New Year's Eve.
In December 1976 they led and went on to win the title -- a feat they repeated in 1978-79, 1979-80, 1982-83, 1983-84, 1987-88, and 1989-90.
Only in 1980-81 and 1990-91 have they been top at New Years Eve then failed to win the championship.

Both Manchester United in 1993-94 and Blackburn in 1994-95 were top at halfway and went on to win the title, while the most spectacular collapse in recent times involved Newcastle last season when they were 12 points ahead of Manchester United -- and finished second, four points behind Alex Ferguson's double winners.
Another team to fall during the second half of the season were Manchester City, who led at the end of 1981 -- and finished 10th the following May.
By the same token only twice in the last 20 seasons has a team lower than second at New Year's Eve come good.
At the turn of 1981 Liverpool were 12th but stormed through the second half of the campaign to win the league. In 1986 they won the League and Cup double after being fourth at the end of December.
This season's title race is widely regarded as one of the most open for years.
Until his team were annihilated 7-1 by Newcastle on Saturday Tottenham's Gerry Francis, whose team were 10th, was saying they still had a chance of winning the league.
That suggestion now looks ridiculous, although odder things have happened in the past.

On December 5 1908 Newcastle lost 9-1 at home to their arch-rivals Sunderland -- but they still won the title by ending the season seven points clear of Everton when a win was still worth only two points.

Newcastle are currently fifth but if they carry on in 1997 the way the ended 1996, not too many teams will be able to stop them taking the title -- and proving a rare exception to the New Year's Eve rule.

As ever, the bookmakers are taking no chances. Following Manchester United's 1-0 win over Leeds on Saturday -- their third in succesion without conceding a goal, Ladbrokes have made them 7-4 joint-favourites with Liverpool to take the title. Arsenal are 9-2, Newcastle 5-1 and Villa 12-1.
